intended_object: The uncentered Hardy–Littlewood maximal function on parabolic space-time ℝ³ × ℝ, with balls taken in the parabolic metric max(|x−y|, √|t−s|) and Lebesgue measure: Mf(z) = sup over balls B ∋ z of (1/|B|)∫_B f. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body takes the supremum over all centres c and radii r of the indicator of the parabolic ball B(c,r), evaluated at z, times the lower-Lebesgue average of f over B(c,r). For r ≤ 0 the ball is empty and the term is 0, so it adds nothing. For r > 0 the ball has positive finite Lebesgue measure and the term is the usual average. So the definition is exactly sup over balls containing z of the average of f, which is the uncentered maximal function.

The balls come from the parabolic pseudometric `parabolicPseudoMetricSpace`, whose distance is max(‖x−y‖₂, √|t−s|) (`dist_eq_parabolicDist`). The measure is the Lebesgue `volume` on `(Fin 3 → ℝ) × ℝ`. This is the standard parabolic maximal function used in Caffarelli–Kohn–Nirenberg-type arguments. Taking f with values in ℝ≥0∞ is the usual choice, and |f| can be plugged in.

The construction does make sense in any metric measure space; the Carleson project has such a general version. But Mathlib has no Hardy–Littlewood maximal function (a grep for maximalFunction or hardyLittlewood in Mathlib finds nothing). The intended object is also the parabolic maximal function on the specific CKN space-time, so the specific setting is part of the object. I therefore judge it faithful, not too narrow.
